title: Autoscaler penalty oscillation causing reserved-pool shortfalls for burst workloads
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: During multiple customer bursts between 2026-03-09T22:00Z and 2026-03-10T02:00Z, several reserved pools failed to scale quickly enough to satisfy transient burst traffic, resulting in SLO breaches and elevated error rates for affected tenants. Affected customers: NimbleDocs, OrbitBI. Symptoms observed: (1) scale-up requests queued but then cancelled by autoscaler, (2) transient headroom went negative for several pools, (3) fallback routing to hosted models activated and increased latency/cost.

Preliminary root cause: A recent heuristic (autoscaler_penalty_v2) intended to penalize noisy tenants interacting with burst credit accounting introduced an unintended feedback loop: when a pool received a quick sequence of burst requests, the heuristic applied a penalty that suppressed follow-up scale-ups for a short window. Combined with an off-by-one in pending_provision accounting, pending nodes were treated as unavailable and autoscaler considered the pool "saturated" and stopped issuing further scale-up operations. The net effect was oscillatory behavior (scale-ups delayed -> queue growth -> increased penalty -> further delay) and under-provisioning at burst onset. Additionally, a regression in headroom calculation caused temporary double-subtraction of burst credits in a subset of multi-tenant pools.

Impact: Two enterprise customers experienced request throttling and degraded tail latency for 17 minutes at peak; internal SLO alerts fired and on-call escalations occurred. Root cause affects Dedicated reserved pools using burst credits; Hosted customers were not impacted.

Investigation artifacts: see links below (PRs, logs, dashboards).
comments: 2026-03-10 — 23:05 UTC — Diego: Triage complete, assigned P0, initiating emergency hotfix branch. Notified SEs for NimbleDocs and OrbitBI; first message postponed to avoid noisy comms until mitigations verified.

2026-03-10 — 23:28 UTC — Ava: Identified autoscaler_penalty_v2 feature flag rollout 2026-03-08 as correlating with incidents. Reproduced oscillation in staging with synthetic burst generator (sim/sim-burst-2026-03-10).

2026-03-10 — 23:55 UTC — Priya (SRE): Applied immediate mitigation: revert autoscaler_penalty_v2 to v1 for affected pools via feature-flag and increased min_stable_window to 60s. Early telemetry shows queue reduction and pending_provision accounting stable.

2026-03-11 — 00:30 UTC — Diego: Hotfix PR opened to fix pending_provision off-by-one and guard headroom calc; PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/12345. Requesting expedited review from infra leads.

2026-03-12 — 09:12 UTC — Engineering: Backfill unit and integration tests added for pending_provision and penalty logic; sim harness extended to run burst scenarios with randomized timing to catch oscillation.
2026-03-12 — 16:40 UTC — Product: Prepared customer comms draft and timeline for NimbleDocs and OrbitBI; scheduled outreach after patch rollout.
resolution: Hotfix deployed to production on 2026-03-12 02:10 UTC which reverts autoscaler_penalty_v2 to previous behavior and fixes pending_provision off-by-one. Initial post-deploy monitors show no recurrence in follow-up bursts. Customer SEs informed and SLO credits discussed.
remediation_plan: 1) Backport hotfix to all active Dedicated clusters and coordinate controlled rollout with capacity windows (ownership: Diego / SRE).
2) Add stable window and hysteresis defaults for autoscaler to prevent oscillation (ownership: Eng Autoscaler team).
3) Correct headroom calc and add property-based tests to prevent regression (ownership: Eng Reliability).
4) Extend simulation harness to run randomized burst workloads nightly and add CI gate for oscillation metric (ownership: Eng QA).
5) Add Grafana alert for 'pool_pending_provision_delta' crossing threshold and a runbook step to temporarily revert penalties (ownership: SRE).
